name: Procedural sound effects
oneLiner: Fourteen game sounds (hit, crit, coin, jump, land, footstep, menu move / confirm / cancel, explosion, laser, power-up, heal, hurt) synthesized live with Web Audio: oscillators, seeded noise, envelopes with attack and release ramps, pitch slides, filters and light FM. Every call is a seeded variation, so repeats never sound copy-pasted; a small mixer caps voices, merges same-frame duplicates, ducks the rest under big sounds and keeps peaks under a soft ceiling. Silent until the player's first click or key, a no-op without Web Audio, and it never touches game state or input. No audio files.
notFor: music (only a duck bus for the game's own music)
sample-accurate rhythm games (sounds start ~5 ms after the call)
realistic foley (this is a stylized 2020s indie palette)

needs: the code that decides each event (jump, land, hit, crit, shot, explosion, pickup, heal, hurt, menu move / confirm / cancel)
a fixed update step in every scene (optional: merge gaps follow game time, ?t= fast-forward stays deterministic)
distance walked per step and on-ground for footsteps (optional)
the event's screen x and the screen width for stereo pan (optional)
provides: sounds through play(preset, {pan | x + width, volume}) and walk(key, dx, grounded)
a mixer: master / sfx volume, mute, max voices with priority stealing, merge of same-preset bursts, ducking (and a music input that ducks)
render(preset, seed) via OfflineAudioContext: the exact samples for tests and waveforms
event records (recent(), onEvent) and stats() for tests and __state()

assets: module/procedural-sfx.js: the element as one dependency-free script (global GameDNA_Sfx): 14 preset recipes, seeded variation, Web Audio builder for live and offline contexts, mixer (voice limit, merge, ducking, compressor, soft ceiling), gesture unlock
no audio, image or font files: every sound is synthesized when it plays
